clue.text: Protection for small area with scrubby vegetation

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a heath is open land covered in heather and scrub

explanation.surface: Someone wants shelter for a small patch of scrubland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover that guards a blade or similar object, so it serves as protection.

clue.text: Restore body part, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: the heel is the back of the foot

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding instruction to mend part of the body, as rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to make well again, bringing a body or wound back to health.

clue.text: They counter poisons, when stationed at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval image: ship's remedies against poison carried by sailors posted at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are remedies that neutralise the effects of a poison in the body.

clue.text: Book about plants devoured by Brother Balthazar

indicators.note: something devoured sits inside the eater, so the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A monk named Balthazar has eaten a botany book.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is an old type of reference volume describing plants and their medicinal uses.

clue.text: Bert and a model going in to marry, having something on which to consummate the union?

definitions.text: something on which to consummate the union

indicators.note: going in tells us one group enters another and sits inside it

parts.note: to wed is to marry

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters to be reshaped

explanation.surface: Bert and his model girlfriend are getting married and need somewhere for the wedding night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun for a fashion model partnering Bert, but it is the signal to rearrange his name with the 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled bed is a cheeky example of a place where newlyweds might complete their marriage.

clue.text: Sow hectare after unusual prediction from the Met Office

indicators.note: unusual signals an odd, irregular version of the letters

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer plans to plant a field after an odd outlook from the meteorologists.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met Office's main public output is the outlook for rain, sun and wind in coming days.

clue.text: Attempt to conceal a piece of clothing in farce

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
taken as written
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: In a stage farce, a character tries to hide an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque mockery of something, a sense close to farce.

clue.text: Strange black American dance

parts.note: rum is an informal British word for odd
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An odd dance from America is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with swaying hip movements.

clue.text: Royal spite misguidedly revealed in letters

indicators.note: misguidedly means going astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal's spiteful remarks come out through published correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistolary describes something carried on through correspondence, like a novel told in a series of written messages.

clue.text: Work into dodgy brie with initially advantageous micro-organisms

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is put inside another
dodgy means unreliable or suspect, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: the cheese, to be rearranged

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of advantageous, also rearranged
to act is to work or function

explanation.surface: Suspect cheese harbouring useful microbes, as in ripening brie.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged cheese letters plus A are split around ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are single-celled living things too small to see without a microscope.

clue.text: Part of body exhibited by drunken setter and tramp

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy crossword setter and a vagrant are showing off some flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder where the arm joins the torso.

clue.text: Apathy led ten to suffer ultimate punishment

indicators.note: to suffer is to be knocked about, so these letters are battered into a new shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Indifference has caused ten people to receive the harshest sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution is the most extreme sentence a court can hand down, so it is the final penalty.

clue.text: Decorative handle for books used in examination

indicators.note: used in tells us these pieces are placed within another word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a handle is slang for a name
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A grand handle for a book is used during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for what a person is called, and 'books' commonly means one of the two Testaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental serves to adorn rather than for practical use.

clue.text: Richmond's opener going in to face the bowling with ill-mannered youth

indicators.note: going in tells us one piece enters another

parts.note: in cricket the batter faces the bowler

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so we keep only the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Richmond

explanation.surface: A cricketer from Richmond goes out to bat alongside a rude youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a cricket opening batsman, but it signals a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved, spoilt child.

clue.text: I lecture about old fashioned handbag

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around and moving them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker announces a talk on a vintage purse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule was a small drawstring bag carried by women in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Arrive heartened by special so-called signs of approval for lipstick etc.

indicators.note: having something put in its heart means one piece takes another into its middle

parts.note: to come is to arrive
S is an abbreviation for special

indicators.note: so-called refers to what something is called, i.e. how it is said

parts.note: ticks are marks showing something is right

explanation.surface: Someone turns up cheered by special marks of approval for their make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is one example of make-up products applied to the face, and 'etc.' widens it to the category.

clue.text: Occupational therapists inhale oxygen, then manage a medical instrument

indicators.note: to inhale is to take something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: OT is short for occupational therapist; plural OTs
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Therapists breathe in oxygen and then handle a clinical tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is a device doctors use to look inside the ear.

clue.text: Strained voice of Scandinavian coming back, carrying paving stone

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so one piece wraps another
coming back means returning the way it came, so the name runs backwards

parts.note: Olaf is a typical Scandinavian name
a sett is a square paving block

explanation.surface: A Norseman returns home lugging a paving slab, his voice strained by the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the high, forced register a male singer uses above his natural range.

clue.text: Island in sea given vessel useful during flooding

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for sea
Noah's ark carried the animals through the Flood

explanation.surface: An island out at sea is given a boat to cope with floods.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small car-free island in the Channel Islands group.

clue.text: End session on computer when record of voyage concludes 'zero fathoms'

parts.note: a ship's log records its voyage
O looks like zero
F is fathom; doubling makes a plural, as with pp for pages

explanation.surface: A ship's logbook ends with a depth reading of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concludes' places the zero and fathoms after the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To log off is to sign out of a computer system at the end of use.

clue.text: Mixed up teens to store hormone

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Confused adolescents are said to hoard a hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: Testosterone is the chief male sex hormone, which surges in teenage boys.

clue.text: Thanks to nonsense shown in cards?

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A sceptic thanks a fortune-teller for the nonsense revealed in the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a pack of illustrated playing cards used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Gala's final result announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by the word's sound

parts.note: fate is the ultimate outcome or destiny

explanation.surface: The outcome of a gala event is being publicly declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gala's' reads as possessive but is 'Gala is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or bazaar, much like a gala day.

clue.text: Spinster missing turn at end of queue gets old thing on which to play music

definitions.text: thing on which to play music

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so one word drops some of its letters

parts.note: an unmarried woman
a spin is a turn

indicators.note: end of points at the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of queue
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman skips her turn at the back of a queue and buys an old record player.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing SPIN from SPINSTER leaves STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system for playing records or recordings through two speakers.

clue.text: A cat is visiting queen to spray!

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tomcat calls on a queen (female cat) in order to mark his territory.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is also a female cat, and toms spray to mark territory, hence the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: These make marching difficult for fat suspect captured by navy

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

parts.note: a fleet is a navy's ships

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so the word is not trusted in its given order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tubby recruit is press-ganged into the navy and struggles on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: People with fallen arches were traditionally thought unfit for long marches in the army.

clue.text: In flat marshy land, a drained settlement is secure

indicators.note: in tells us the following pieces sit inside another word

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshland
taken as written

indicators.note: drained means emptied, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of settlement

explanation.surface: A village in drained fenland is safe from flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying drained marshland in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to fix or attach something firmly, which is to secure it.
